summary: Discovery call with SparrowMetrics to understand migration drivers from OpenAI/Azure and on-prem inference stacks (vLLM/TGI). They are evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for a mix of PII-sensitive user queries and higher-throughput batch scoring. Key concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, model compatibility (TGI/vLLM artifacts), KV cache behavior, SSO/KMS integration, and rollout strategy. Agreed next steps include pricing, security docs, and a technical deep dive + benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11 08:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Silva (SparrowMetrics HoML), Jordan Lee (Platform Eng), Aditi Rao (Security)

[00:00] Emily Chen: hi everyone thanks for doing this, quick intro - im emily, on the account team at Redwood. ravi is our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta Silva: hey thanks emily, doing good. we are eager to see how redwood fits, um we've been running most of our prod on openai and a few on azure openai, plus a couple of internal vLLM pools for batch scoring.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: yeah, we built some adapters to TGI for fine-tuned models - it's kinda janky but works.
[00:24] Ravi Patel: cool, thanks for the context. high level question -- are you primarily trying to reduce cost, improve latency, or get better control/security? or all three?
[00:34] Marta Silva: all three, but order varies by workload. For interactive chat features, latency and reliability are top. For nightly batch embeddings and reranking it's cost. And for a new government pilot we need VPC/HSM certs.
[00:50] Aditi Rao: i can add, security is non-negotiable for the pilot - we need KMS-backed key control, auditable logs, and ideally on-prem or private VPC options.
[01:05] Emily Chen: makes sense. quick note - redwood supports hosted for rapid dev, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads. we can talk tradeoffs as we go.
[01:17] Jordan Lee: curious about artifact compatibility - we use models exported for vLLM and TGI endpoints. will those load with minimal changes?
[01:24] Ravi Patel: good question. short answer: we ingest most standard HF-style checkpoints and container artifacts, but there are differences with some TGI-specific tokenizers and custom kernels. we'll need to review a sample model artifact to confirm. generally we maintain a model catalog and will propose a variant if quantization or kernel selection is needed.
[01:45] Marta Silva: okay, that aligns with our expectations. what about the KV cache behavior? we rely heavily on long context in chat and reuse past tokens for cheap.
[01:56] Ravi Patel: our runtime has prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; it tries to keep KV cache hot for pinned conversational flows. caveat: the savings depend on your session stickiness and shard placement. when customers run cross-region traffic it can evaporate.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: so is that automatic or a config we set per-route?
[02:16] Ravi Patel: both. auto heuristics plus per-route policies. you can pin model versions and cache TTLs.
[02:22] Marta Silva: great — could you give rough numbers on latency and cost versus openai for a 4k context model?
[02:29] Emily Chen: rough ballpark: hosted can be similar-ish latency to OpenAI for conversational MLPs, dedicated often drops p95 by 20-40% depending on GPU class and batching; unit cost on dedicated or private with quantization is typically 30-60% lower for heavy token workloads but varies. we'll share a detailed worksheet.
[02:50] Aditi Rao: about encryption - does redwood integrate with our cloud KMS and HSM? we prefer customer-managed keys.
[02:57] Ravi Patel: yes, Private and Dedicated support customer KMS. For Private on-prem we also support HSM integrations. We will need an infra diagram to map key wrapping, and we do audit logs.
[03:14] Marta Silva: any SOC2 or ISO attestations?
[03:17] Emily Chen: we are SOC2 Type II and have an enterprise security pack we can share.
[03:21] Jordan Lee: can we talk about the migration flow - we have a lot of pipelines tied to OpenAI APIs, function-calling, and streaming. How hard is it to port those?
[03:32] Ravi Patel: streaming plus function/tool calling are supported. The SDKs match typical REST patterns, but there are slight differences in streaming chunk formats and some function call metadata. Usually it's a small adapter in code - we've helped customers port with a few lines per integration. For large fleets we provide migration guides and a compatibility shim.
[03:50] Marta Silva: ok that's promising. we're also concerned about eval parity — we run an internal RAG evaluation and quality metrics; will outputs match closely or will prompts need to be retuned?
[03:59] Ravi Patel: parity depends on the exact model family and sampling defaults. If you're moving from a hosted OpenAI model to a similar open checkpoint we can get very close but often need small prompt/temperature tweaks. we run automated regressions against your eval set to detect drift.
[04:18] Emily Chen: the typical approach we recommend: run a small A/B with traffic split, collect metrics, tweak prompts or quantization, then scale. can also pin fallback to the old provider during rollout for safety.
[04:33] Jordan Lee: fallback - how does routing and fallback work?
[04:36] Ravi Patel: routing policies can be latency-first or cost-first; we have automatic fallback to a compatible variant or upstream provider if capacity is constrained. you configure per-route SLOs and fallback chains.
[04:47] Marta Silva: nice - what's the time to onboard if we start a pilot? we have a feature launch in 8 weeks and want to know if we can run a pilot in parallel.
[04:56] Emily Chen: 8 weeks is tight but doable: week 1-2 onboarding + infra eval, week 3 perf/compat sample runs, week 4-6 pilot with A/B, week 7-8 roll or expand. depends on how fast you can share model artifacts and perf traces.
[05:12] Aditi Rao: also we need to validate SSO and RBAC - do you support SAML/IdP, SCIM?
[05:17] Ravi Patel: yes we support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: can you run our TGI container images or do we need to export?
[05:27] Ravi Patel: for private on-prem we can run customer containers with some guardrails. For hosted/dedicated we usually ingest image artifacts into our runtime and may request an HF-style package. We'll produce a compatibility checklist.
[05:38] Marta Silva: pricing orientation - our procurement will want line-of-sight into committed spend vs pay-as-you-go.
[05:45] Emily Chen: we offer usage-based hosted, monthly reserved for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. We'll send a few scenarios based on your throughput and token mix.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: about benching, we use both latency SLOs and quality thresholds. can you help run parity benchmarks with our prompts?
[05:59] Ravi Patel: yes, we do benchmark runs. we'll need your sample prompts, a small eval corpus, and a representative request trace so we can simulate batch and interactive mixes.
[06:12] Marta Silva: ok i'll have that prepared. one more, how do you handle model updates? we have a strict change control process and need canary rollouts and audit trail.
[06:21] Ravi Patel: rollout policies include canary percentages, automatic regressions on eval sets, and audit logs for model versioning. You can pin live traffic to older model versions until the rollout completes.
[06:33] Aditi Rao: what about data retention - do you persist raw user inputs on hosted? we need options to not retain PII.
[06:40] Emily Chen: we provide configurable retention policies; for PII you can opt for zero retention on hosted or choose Private where data never leaves your VPC.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: any limits for concurrency per model on Dedicated?
[06:54] Ravi Patel: Dedicated pools are sized; concurrency depends on GPU class and batch settings. we'll run sizing with your QPS and p95 goals.
[07:05] Marta Silva: perfect. can you walk through a little of the technical nitty gritty — how do you handle kernel selection for quantized LoRA-style models?
[07:14] Ravi Patel: our compilation layer selects kernels by architecture, sequence length distribution, and quantization scheme. for LoRA/fine-tune overlays we apply merges at load time and pick quantization-friendly execution paths. occasionally some custom ops trigger fallbacks to slower kernels — we flag those during onboarding.
[07:34] Jordan Lee: we've had issues with OOM when using dynamic batching with vLLM; do you have safeguards?
[07:40] Ravi Patel: yes, the runtime has back-pressure and request shaping; we also allow per-queue memory caps to avoid noisy neighbor OOMs.
[07:50] Marta Silva: are there examples of companies who transitioned from Azure OpenAI to Redwood and kept similar latency?
[07:56] Emily Chen: yes, a couple of customers in analytics did a migration; we can share redacted benchmarks.
[08:02] Jordan Lee: when you say redacted, do you mean public case studies?
[08:06] Emily Chen: some public, some under NDA. we'll share relevant ones based on your consent.
[08:12] Marta Silva: ok, let's talk risk — if we move traffic and see a quality regression, what's the rollback window and SLA implications?
[08:20] Ravi Patel: you can instantly route back to the previous provider via our fallback chain. SLA depends on contract; during pilot we typically run no-SLA evaluation, but enterprise Dedicated comes with uptime SLAs.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: curious, what's the process for model-specific performance tuning, like sequence-length optimizations?
[08:40] Ravi Patel: we'll profile your request distribution, recommend token limits, batching, and sequence length padding strategies. sometimes model pruning or quantization profiles improve throughput with minimal quality loss.
[08:55] Marta Silva: good. any caveats around function calling and structured outputs?
[08:59] Ravi Patel: we support function/tool calling; structured output is supported but schema differences may require slight adapter logic. Also streaming of function calls differs a bit from other providers.
[09:10] Aditi Rao: what's your incident response for potential data exposure?
[09:14] Emily Chen: we have an incident response plan, customer notification windows, and forensic logs. for private deployments we can align with your IR runbooks.
[09:24] Marta Silva: ok looks like we have alignment on the big items. would you be able to run a short tech deep dive next Wednesday?
[09:30] Emily Chen: yes we can schedule a 60-min deep dive — ravi will lead and bring infra bench lead.
[09:36] Jordan Lee: sounds good. can you also include a checklist of required artifacts we need to give you?
[09:40] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll include: model artifacts, sample prompts/eval set, request traces, infra network constraints, and encryption/KMS requirements.
[09:48] Marta Silva: perfect. any open questions from your side?
[09:51] Emily Chen: just to confirm timelines — can you share when the procurement window opens and the pilot target date?
[09:57] Marta Silva: procurement starts late May, product launch mid-June; pilot ideally mid-late April to validate.
[10:06] Emily Chen: understood. we'll follow up with docs and schedule the deep dive. thanks everyone.

Post-call notes:
- Customer is multi-workload: interactive chat (latency sensitive), batch embeddings (cost sensitive), regulated pilot (security-sensitive).
- Key asks: compatibility with TGI/vLLM artifacts, KV cache behavior, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 docs, pricing scenarios, and a technical deep dive + benchmark.
- Agreed deliverables: Dedicated sizing worksheet, perf parity checklist, security pack, scheduling of deep dive.

End of transcript.
